pr_title: Add validation that all targets used as platforms actually advertise

issue_context.title: Cycle error when --platforms is not a platform
issue_context.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

If you try to use a number of things as a platform, you get a massive garbage error from the cycle detector.

Examples include:
* `sh_binary`
* `rust_binary`
* `config_setting`

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

This can be reproduced in the repo at https://github.com/m3rcuriel/bazel/tree/cycle_repro by running `bazel build //... --platforms=//:garbage` or even `bazel build //... --platforms=//:test`.

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

5.3.7.b-3-hardened #1 SMP PREEMPT @1572019254 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

`release 0.29.1- (@non-git)`

### If `bazel info release` returns "development version" or "(@non-git)", tell us how you built Bazel.

This version comes from the AUR. Also fails with bazel HEAD (11/20/19) built with the bazel from AUR.

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin ; git rev-parse master ; git rev-parse HEAD` ?

```
git@github.com:bazelbuild/bazel
2b7e21db100bdc0bd319f37106ed3d9e7c8dbe74
2b7e21db100bdc0bd319f37106ed3d9e7c8dbe74
```

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

Inspired by https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_rust/issues/267.

review_comments: I don't quite understand why you don't return here if values are missing.

This is a source of many Skyframe errors: you have to propagate errors *before* you restart due to missing dependencies, or else the errors will be swallowed and either a) not ever be raised, or b) be raised for the parent of the current skyfunction call. Neither of these is good, and so checking for errors first is essential.

In the simple one-key `env.getValueOrThrow` case this happens automatically, because the `getValueOrThrow` method throws the error immediately and your exception handler catches it, but when requesting multiple keys at once via `env.getValuesOrThrow` it is surprisingly difficult to get it right.

This is why all of my skyfunctions have a lot of error-testing code, because I've been bitten by this too many times **and I still get it wrong the first time**.
Ugh. I'll reserve my rant about this for another time. :)
It might be useful to add a comment here why this exception cannot happen/can safely be ignored.
